name: Mahindra Logistics Ltd
title: Mahindra Logistics Ltd - 540768 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Turnaround logistics story: FY26 reported PAT ₹2.3 crore vs ₹35.8 crore loss, Express GM positive at 1.3% but still EBITDA-negative (₹31 crore loss); management gives no hard EBITDA timeline.

summary.headline: Mahindra Logistics returned to profit in Q4 FY26, with reported PAT of INR20.2 crores versus a INR6.7 crores loss a year earlier.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 14% YoY to INR1,791 crores and gross margin expanded to 10.5% from 9.5%. Adjusted EBITDA (after deducting long-term lease rent) rose to INR57 crores, a 3.2% margin versus 2.4% a year earlier. Full-year reported PAT was INR2.3 crores against a INR35.8 crores loss in FY25, after a Q3 exceptional gratuity charge under the new Labour Codes. Express (MESPL) remained EBITDA-negative for FY26 but gross-margin positive for the full year and close to EBITDA breakeven per management. Freight forwarding faces West Asia-related headwinds going into FY27.

segments.name: Contract Logistics
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR1,381 crores (+12% YoY); FY26 revenue INR5,490 crores (+16%) and reported EBITDA INR389 crores (+24% vs INR314 crores). Management cites gross margin growth of 19% in Q4 from exiting non-profitable customers.

segments.name: Express (MESPL)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 49% YoY; FY26 revenue INR449 crores (+25%), gross margin 1.3% for the full year. Quarterly GM rose from INR20 lakh in Q2 to INR2.7 crores in Q3 and INR6.6 crores in Q4. FY26 EBITDA loss INR31 crores vs INR51 crores loss in FY25.

segments.name: Freight Forwarding
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR89 crores (+17% YoY); gross margin +50% YoY. FY26 revenue grew 14%, EBITDA INR10.1 crores vs INR6.8 crores in FY25. Q4 growth is now facing West Asia-related headwinds.

segments.name: Mobility
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR386 crores (+22% vs INR316 crores). Q4 revenue grew 42% YoY and gross margin 17% YoY; growth driven by large B2B accounts, with utilisation improvement a focus on the asset-heavy Alyte Prive premium offering in Delhi.

segments.name: Last-mile delivery
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR72 crores (-18% YoY, from INR89 crores) after deliberate site exits. Gross margin rose to INR6.5 crores in Q4 from INR2.7 crores in Q3; EBITDA moved from a INR1 crore loss in Q3 to a INR2.2 crore profit in Q4.

guidance_outlook: Express: management is targeting mid-to-high teens revenue growth; it will not give a timeline for EBITDA breakeven but says it is 'very close'.
Express: management said it will invest in technology in FY27 after two years of limited tech investment.
White space: target to reduce by 95% (from 1.6 million sq ft at start of FY26 to 0.7 million at year-end) by September 2026; management says it is on or slightly ahead of the glide path.
Last-mile: management says all pruning was completed in FY26 and no further reduction is expected.
Contract logistics: one new segment to be entered in FY27 from two being evaluated; name not disclosed.
Management declined to give forward guidance on margins or PAT, and gave no FY27 revenue target.
capex_capacity: White space reduced by 3 lakh sq ft in Q4 and 9 lakh sq ft in FY26; contract logistics warehousing footprint fell from about 20.4 million sq ft in Q3 to about 19 million sq ft in Q4 per analyst data.
Lease exits and early terminations generated a INR14.38 crore ROU reversal gain, which management said reflects site-level business decisions.
Technology investment planned for FY27 in the Express business.
Express is a network business; management compares its economics to an airline, with heavy upfront costs.
demand_pricing: Express volume growth stated as mid-to-high teens YoY; management has stopped disclosing absolute volumes.
Express yields improved through specific price corrections with certain clients, not a blanket price increase; favourable mix also contributed.
Retail (e-commerce) express demand is outperforming B2B in recent quarters; e-commerce is growing faster within Express.
Consolidation in the Express market (a competitor absorbed by Delhivery) is seen as supporting pricing discipline, per the management.
Freight forwarding is under pressure from West Asia conflict: shipping disruption, higher freight rates, insurance premiums and surcharges, and customers delaying decisions.
Management said a diesel price rise of 10-15% would be passed through to customers 100% with no lag, but flagged possible macro inflation impact.
Consolidated e-commerce and quick-commerce revenue exceeds INR1,000 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What is Express volume growth, and can it sustain mid-teens revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Express volume growth is mid-to-high teens YoY, and that a mid-teens revenue growth target is achievable. Volume is no longer disclosed alone as it is not a sufficient metric without yield.

qa_highlights.question: Is adjusted EBITDA margin likely to surpass the pre-Ind AS FY18-19 levels of about 3.6-3.9%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it agreed directionally but gave no forward guidance and said the turnaround has only just started.

qa_highlights.question: When will Express reach EBITDA breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EBITDA breakeven is the immediate goal and it is 'very close', but gave no timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Are there further last-mile pruning or declines to expect?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said all last-mile pruning was done in FY26 and the business is now expected to grow with profitable clients.

qa_highlights.question: Are there similar receivable provisions expected? What drove the INR28 crore credit provision?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the provision reflects prudence on aged receivables under management judgment. She said nothing similar warrants provisioning at present.

qa_highlights.question: Is the West Asia conflict affecting other segments, and how would a fuel price spike affect the business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said only Freight Forwarding is affected so far; other segments are on plan. A 10-15% diesel rise would be passed through immediately, but management flagged broader economic inflation risk.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Express industry yield, and what share of Express revenue is e-commerce?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to share industry-level yield comparisons or the e-commerce share of Express revenue, citing competitive sensitivity.

risks_watch: Freight forwarding margins and volumes under West Asia-related shipping, freight and insurance pressure; management expects headwinds to persist in the near term.
Express remains EBITDA-negative (FY26 loss INR31 crores); breakeven timing not given.
Diesel price increases could spread macro inflation even if passed through to customers.
Last-mile revenue fell 18% YoY in Q4; management says pruning is complete but growth is not yet shown.
Receivable provisions (INR28 crores credit provision) and whether more are needed.
Rent-adjusted EBITDA margin is still only 3.2%; adjusted-basis disclosure is new and may not be comparable with prior periods.
White space commitment: September 2026 completion of the 95% reduction.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the turnaround and the return to profit, with specific figures given. Cautious on freight forwarding and the macro picture, and evasive on Express timelines, margin targets, volume figures, yields and utilisation, which it declined to quantify.
key_quotes: After 2 years of losses, our return to PAT profitability marks more than a milestone.
Our focus here is on improving the utilization level for the asset-heavy part of the business, which is Alyte Prive, our premium B2B offering that we offer right now in Delhi.
Our focus continues to remain on EBITDA improvement with PAT progression to follow in a calibrated manner.
we are very close to an EBITDA positive number.

growth.why: Express guided to mid-to-high teens revenue and volume growth for FY27 with no capacity or order numbers behind it, while management gave no company-wide FY27 revenue target and flagged West Asia headwinds in freight forwarding; white space reduction (95% by Sep 2026) is a shrinking footprint, not added capacity.
